title: Scoring table
subject: Science
unit: Spring 1: Forces, magnets and light (Mighty Metals and Why Do Cat's Eyes Glow at Night?)
source: Seeded from science/y3 lesson 16 (Scoring table (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 16: Reflection: testing reflective materials. To understand that shiny and light-coloured surfaces reflect light well

questions.q: Which reflects more: white paper or black paper?
questions.model: Think: light or dark colour? White is light. Light colours reflect more light. So white paper reflects more.

questions.q: Why are reflective strips useful on a school bag?
questions.a: They reflect car lights so drivers can see you.

questions.q: Name the fair-test thing we change.
Core: In a dim room, shine a torch on 5 materials (foil, white paper, black fabric, a spoon, cardboard). Score each 1 (dull) to 5 (very bright).
questions.a: Pupils' own; foil and spoon score highest, black fabric lowest.
questions.model: Teacher shows the first: torch 30 cm away, shine on foil, it is very bright: score 5.

questions.q: Extend: Which material would you put on a coat for walking at night? Why?
questions.a: A shiny reflective strip or foil-like material: it reflects the most light.

questions.q: Stretch: Why does a mirror show a clear picture but foil does not?
questions.a: The mirror is very smooth, so light bounces back evenly; crumpled foil scatters it.

questions.q: Big question: which materials are best for keeping walkers safe in the dark?
questions.a: Shiny, light or reflective materials such as reflective strips.
